subject.title: [Bug]: Managed Memory Dreaming Promotion cron silently NO_REPLY since 2026-05-09 (jobs.json lastRun stays null)

question: How should managed Memory Dreaming Promotion report per-workspace failure or no-op sweeps after the SQLite migrations: cron error/degraded status, Dreaming diagnostics only, or current ok-with-logs behavior?
rationale: Current code can handle internal Dreaming failures while cron records the outer run, so the right end state is a product/operations semantics choice rather than a purely mechanical bug fix.

options.title: Expose Degraded Dreaming Status
options.body: Treat failed or no-op managed Dreaming sweeps as an operator-visible degraded/error diagnostic in cron, doctor, or the Dreaming surface so silent data gaps are discoverable.

options.title: Keep Cron Ok, Improve Dreams Diagnostics
options.body: Leave cron status tied to the outer run and add clearer Dreaming-specific diagnostics for stale diary or failed workspace counts.

options.title: Close After Live Non-Repro
options.body: If maintainers can live-verify current release no longer misses diary output or state updates, close this as fully fixed by the SQLite migration.

recommendation.title: Expose Degraded Dreaming Status
recommendation.body: Treat failed or no-op managed Dreaming sweeps as an operator-visible degraded/error diagnostic in cron, doctor, or the Dreaming surface so silent data gaps are discoverable.

likelyOwner.reason: The remaining decision crosses the SQLite state migration, memory-core Dreaming, and cron/operator-status boundary that steipete recently changed in PR 91056.
